title: Responsible Growth: an agenda for the Commission's first 100 days and beyond (2027)
label: GCV's 501(c)(4) agenda
relationship: Georgia Conservation Voters is a 501(c)(4) advocacy organization. Its affiliated 501(c)(3), the Georgia Conservation Voters Education Fund, sponsors this site.
source: Georgia Conservation Voters, 2027 Responsible Growth agenda for the Public Service Commission, shared with us by GCV. Read November 23, 2026.

items.ask: For customers using more than 100 MW, such as data centers, enforce minimum bills, financial guarantees, upfront contributions and protections if a customer leaves. Review whether current contracts and Georgia Power's financial backstop protect other customers if projected demand falls short, and require findings on cost risk before approving more generation or other major investments.

Set up regular public reporting of projected and actual large-customer demand, infrastructure costs, contract performance and effects on residential rates, and require Georgia Power to show whether customers get the benefits it projected.

Carry the Real-Time Pricing investigation through to decide whether large customers get fuel credits or other pricing benefits at the expense of residential and small-business customers, and correct any cost allocation the evidence does not support.

Weigh new gas plants, coal plant extensions and other major generation against efficiency, solar, storage, demand response and other supply, with open cost and reliability comparisons, competitive bids and independent evaluation.
items.when: 2027 review and the 2028 Integrated Resource Plan

items.ask: Review Georgia Power's EASE program and other efficiency programs, tracking households served, verified energy savings and bill savings, especially for low-income customers, and consider demand response as an alternative to new plants.
items.when: 2027 program review and the 2028 Integrated Resource Plan

items.ask: Set clearer interconnection standards for rooftop solar and storage, review what customers are paid for power they send to the grid, and name barriers that need action by the General Assembly.

Look at tariffs and contract terms that would have large users cut demand at peak times, pay for standby capacity and supply their own power where appropriate, judged on reliability, cost and environmental effects.

Open a proceeding on disconnection protections during extreme heat or cold, medical emergencies and other hardship, reviewing notice, reconnection and PrePay rules, with public reporting of disconnections and reconnections.

Review Georgia Power's income-qualified bill discount: how many eligible customers it reaches, whether the discount is enough, and simpler enrollment, weighing funding and cost allocation before any change.
Start a proceeding on itemized bills that show fuel, storm and other major charges, and give plain-language estimates of bill effects before major votes.
Have fuel purchasing, natural gas hedging, storm recovery and other major charges independently reviewed, and exclude costs that do not meet recovery standards.
Keep cost studies, demand forecasts, large-customer contracts, financial guarantees and models available for review in the 2028 rate case and resource plan, with protection for confidential records.
